additional_info.subject: Software Update Siemens Ladesäulen
additional_info.body:
Guten Tag,
wir haben bei einer unserer Ladesäulen (VxUVaS) bemerkt, dass viele Ladevorgänge mit 0 kWh geladener Energiemenge in unseren CDRs auftauchen.
Da ist mir aufgefallen, dass alle unsere Ladesäulen noch auf der Softwareversion sind, mit der sie ausgeliefert wurden (
v7.0.5-0-gd66ba3a+FileHandlerHF (PRODUCTION))
.
Wir haben versucht die Ladesäulen über unser Backend (eRound) auf die neuste dort verfügbare Softwareversion (
Siemens V11 OCPP16 Version 78)
zu updaten, dies ist aber leider gescheitert.
Besteht die Möglichkeit, dass Sie die Ladesäulen aus der Ferne updaten? Folgende Ladesäulen benötigen ein Update: Ojtpa9, VxUVaS, GniUnx. Vielen Dank!

additional_info.subject: Re: ID0455209-DC/Si-D/DE-[multi] Software update CRM:03056000158
additional_info.body:
Good afternoon Mr. Siebrecht,
Apologies for the late reply. I analyzed the logs at the timestamp you provided me:
It seems the failed sessions are caused by a wrong handling of the authentication phase from the end user.
From our Siemens Backend, I see the following configuration in terms of OCPP IDs of the outlets:
The outlet DC1 (left outlet) is shown on the HMI as outlet 1, but it is identified on the App with ID:3
The same goes for outlet DC2 (right outlet), on the HMI is shown as outlet 3, but it is identified on the App with ID:1.
What happened therefore is two failed sessions:
In the first case the user authorized via app outlet 3 (which on the backend is configured for DC1), but plugged in DC2.
In the second case the user authorized via app outlet 1 (which on the backend is configured for DC2) and plugged in DC1:
In conclusion, the sessions failed due to wrong authorization process from user. However, I must say such configuration of the outlets could lead to some confusion in the user.
Please let me know if the OCPP Connector ID should be rectified from Siemens side.
Looking forward to hearing feedback from you soon!
With kind regards,

additional_info.subject: Re: ID0455209-DC/Si-D/DE-[multi] Software update CRM:03056000158
additional_info.body:
Good morning Mr. Siebrecht,
Thank you very much for the prompt feedback! I took time to analyze the two 0kWh sessions you reported in your previous email, and these are my findings:
Charger VxUVaS - 12.11.2025
​​​​​​​
The EV was connected on DC2 at 2025-11-12T15:24:27 and authorized via RFID (no confusing outlet IDs in this case).
The charging session started at 2025-11-12T15:25:10, and was stopped after via RFID after 16 minutes at 2025-11-12T15:41:01
Unfortunately, this is a real 0kWh session, as the meterstop value communicated in the StopTransaction equals the meterstart value communicated in the StartTransaction message:
2025-11-12T15:24:31 OCPP: Send command: StartTransaction (3cccf0e0-ca3c-4ab6-8aa9-df8f778274ab) - {"connectorId":1,"idTag":"049D96120C2090","meterStart":
6532380
,"timestamp":"2025-11-12T15:24:31.051Z"}
2025-11-12T15:41:15.OCPP: Send command: StopTransaction (7a96dfe6-e450-4292-890e-13f6ef87a3c4) - {"meterStop":
6532380
,"timestamp":"2025-11-12T15:41:15.255Z"
This is an issue on ERK chargers in regards of the OCMF data information, happening randomly. This is possible to see it in the logs as it is reported that the OCMF record is invalid:
2025-11-12T15:41:15.253319+00:00 [FW080005G1] sicharge-cp [local0:err] sicharge-cp-backend/c99bb65efba9[847]: OCMF record is invalid:
The good news is, this issue has already been addressed by our R&D, and
it will be fixed in the next FW release
. The FW
v8.1.X
will be released in CW48 (end of next week)
Charger GniUnx - 13.11.2025
​​​​​​​
Failed session happened on AC socket, which was not able to start the session.
The issue was not related to the OCPP Connector Id, as it did not change and was always
2
, but it seems to be related to the communication with AC meter.
It could also be that the issue is related to the AC cable used by the customer, but I do not have proof for this.
I will escalate the issue to our R&D department for clarification of the behavior on the AC socket, and provide you feedback asap.
I will provide you with feedback soon!
Looking forward to hearing from you soon!
With kind regards,

additional_info.subject: Re: ID0455209-DC/Si-D/DE-[multi] Software update CRM:03056000158
additional_info.body:
Good afternoon Mr. Siebrecht,
I analyzed the logs at the timestamp you mentioned. I believe that the issue is still on the OCPP Connector ID, but on the Backend side.
Yesterday we changed the OCPP Connector ID from Charger side, but I believe this has to be cross-checked with the configuration the Backend has for the outlets.
Let me show you what I mean from the logs:
First session 18.11.2025 13:13
RemoteStartTransaction received for outlet id
3
, DC2 connected and the session started correctly, and was stopped at 2025-11-18T12:40:51 (13:40 CET time)
The session itself worked from charger point of view, as it was authenticated for outlet 3 and Dc2 was connected.
What I believe is that in the Backend outlet 3 is still configured for DC1, hence you do not see any energy transfer.
Second session 17.11.2025 20:25
RFID is scanned for outlet 1 (DC1), DC1 is then connected and the session started as well.
Again, probably in the Backend was not registered
Sessions on 17.11.2025 18:26
In this case, the customer was plugging in DC2 (right outlet), but scanning the RFID after selecting DC1 outlet.
Once he authorized via app, the charging session was successful.
I apologize if this change of configuration created issues from Backend side.
Please let me know if you can modify the outlet configuration from Backend side, otherwise I will proceed to bring back the original configuration of OCPP connector IDs from charger side.
In case the original configuration has to be restored, please let me know if only for this charger or also for the other two.
Looking forward to hearing feedback from you.
​​​​​​​Thank you
With kind regards,
